name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise (3-Second Eccentric)
description: The seated lateral raise with a 3-second eccentric phase lowers each repetition over 3 full seconds, dramatically increasing total time under tension for the medial deltoid and potentially enhancing muscle damage (a primary hypertrophy mechanism). The seated position prevents the torso swing that often contaminates standing lateral raises, ensuring the eccentric is performed with strict medial deltoid engagement throughout.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at the sides. Sit upright.
execution.setup_instructions: Use lighter weight than a standard lateral raise — the slow eccentric is significantly more fatiguing.
steps: Step 1: Raise both arms laterally to shoulder height (1-2 seconds up).
Step 2: At the top, hold 1 second.
Step 3: Lower both arms over exactly 3 seconds — count it.
Step 4: Return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale raising. Inhale through the 3-second lowering.
common_mistakes: Lowering faster than 3 seconds — time the descent with a count
Using standard lateral raise weight — reduce load by 20-30%
safety_considerations: Light loads — the eccentric focus amplifies the stimulus
coaching_cues: Count one, two, three on the way down
No dropping — keep control the entire descent
